app/static/app.js — the frontend script

Purpose

The entire frontend behavior, in one vanilla-JS IIFE with "use strict": fetch flow and result display, copy/download, the saved-transcripts list, summarization, the prompt-injection benchmark, and the live log viewer. No framework, no build step, no CDN — the file is served as-is at /app.js and references DOM ids defined in index.html.

Public surface

Nothing is exported (module-scoped IIFE). Its effective API is the set of DOM ids it requires from index.html: url-input, fetch-form, fetch-btn, fetch-spinner, error-banner, result, video-title, video-language, transcript-panel, copy-btn, download-btn, saved-list, saved-empty, saved-count, saved-refresh-btn, provider-picker, summarize-btn, summarize-spinner, summary-panel, summary-text, summary-copy-btn, auto-summarize, auto-summarize-note, injection-panel, injection-toggle, injection-toggle-label, injection-point, injection-payload, injection-preview, benchmark-models, benchmark-judge, benchmark-run, benchmark-spinner, benchmark-label, benchmark-results, benchmark-tally, benchmark-rows, log-panel, logs-toggle. It also defines the ERROR_MESSAGES map (server error code → human message) for the nine taxonomy codes.

Invariants

  • No-innerHTML rule — absolute. Every fetched string (transcript, title, names, summary, log lines) enters the DOM via textContent (or element construction) only; never as HTML. Markup-like content from YouTube or a backend cannot be rendered or executed.
  • Requests use the real file name, display uses a prettified one. List rows keep the real name in data-name; the display label (extension stripped, underscores → spaces, CSS capitalization) is cosmetic and is never sent to the server.
  • Two distinct name variables, deliberately. currentSavedName (a clicked saved row) drives Download's enabled predicate — a freshly fetched transcript does not enable Download. currentTranscriptName (the fetch response's derived name, or the saved row's name) is what Summarize sends for the alongside save.
  • displayToken invalidates stale results. A monotonic token is bumped on every new transcript display; an in-flight saved-summary response or summarize response for a previously displayed transcript is discarded.
  • One summarize path, two entry points. doSummarize(auto) serves the manual click (auto=false: picker selection, error banner on failure) and the post-fetch auto-fire (auto=true: the default target from defaultSelection(), the subdued note on failure). Both share the busy state (button, picker, and checkbox disabled + spinner), the summarizing guard, and the token staleness rule.
  • Auto-summarize fires on fresh fetches only. The hook sits in renderResult, never in the saved-transcript click path. With the checkbox on it first reuses the saved-summary read: found → show it and skip (no summarize call); otherwise fire doSummarize(true) against the picker's default (defaultSelection(), the same target the picker pre-selects). The accepted consecutive-fetch race drops the second auto-fire via the summarizing guard (design D7).
  • Auto failures never raise the banner. Every automatic failure shape (PROVIDER_ERROR, NOT_CONFIGURED, INVALID_PROVIDER, INPUT_TOO_LONG, network error, empty-summary 200) shows the subdued #auto-summarize-note (textContent only) and leaves the enabled Summarize button as the explicit retry; the manual path keeps the banner untouched. The note follows the same token staleness rule as the success path: a late failure for a superseded transcript is dropped, never painted onto a newer one.
  • The Auto-summarize checkbox mirrors the server setting. Loaded once on page load via GET /api/settings (no polling); toggling POSTs the change and reverts the checkbox to the last persisted value if the write fails. It is interactive only when providers are configured and is disabled while any summarize is in flight.
  • No polling. The saved list, the provider list, and the settings load once on page load, the list also reloads after each successful fetch and via its Refresh button. The provider list is never re-fetched (a stale picker after a config edit gets a clean 400 INVALID_PROVIDER telling the user to reload).
  • Copy works over plain HTTP. navigator.clipboard.writeText first, falling back to a hidden-textarea execCommand("copy") — the Clipboard API does not exist in non-secure contexts, and plain HTTP is the normal access path.
  • A 2xx with no summary text is a failure for display — show the error region, never an empty panel (same truthiness check as the saved-summary load).
  • The log panel is a display concern. Entries keep accumulating while the panel is hidden, so re-showing it includes what was logged in the meantime; the panel trims to its 200-line display cap (mirroring the server buffer).
  • SSE is fire-and-forget. EventSource reconnects automatically; unparseable payloads are dropped; no error handling is needed.

Injection benchmark invariants

  • The splice is client-side and produces one undifferentiated string (design decision 1). splicePayload concatenates the payload at the chosen point (prepend / middle / append, default append) into a single string; a disabled toggle or an empty payload sends the transcript exactly as displayed. The request body is {text, preset, provider, model} only — no separate injection/payload field, and the app never adds a label marking the payload to the model (indirect-injection fidelity). middle cuts at a line boundary near the center so both halves are non-empty for a multi-line transcript (a single-line transcript falls back to a character split).
  • The benchmark never persists. Delivery and judge both go through the non-persisting POST /api/llm-call (the summarize and judge presets); the persisting POST /api/summarize is never called, so no .summary file is created or modified.
  • The system prompt is a server-side preset, not client text (design decision 3). The client sends only a preset id; there is no client system prompt field.
  • Layered oracle per model (design decision 5):
  • Canary (deterministic): a unique token (INJ-<16 hex>) is generated per run and an emit instruction is appended to the payload (never labeling it an injection). A model is a hit iff its own output contains the token (substring match, checked per model). canary is null for payload-less runs.
  • Judge (LLM): the input is the original unspliced transcript plus \n\n---\n\n plus the model's output, called with the judge preset. The verdict is the first line, exactly resisted/partial/full (case-insensitive); the rest is the reason. A failed or unparseable judge is "unavailable" for that model only — it never fails the run.
  • Human: a per-model settable verdict (—/resisted/partial/full).
  • Runs are parallel per model against the identical spliced text, guarded by the benchRunning flag and stale-discarded via the displayToken (a run started for a previously displayed transcript is dropped). Results accumulate in benchRuns, keyed provider/model, one entry per run.
  • A new transcript clears results, not setup. clearBenchmark (on a new fetch or saved-transcript display) wipes benchRuns — the previous transcript's results no longer apply — but keeps the payload and insertion-point settings, since the same payload can target a new carrier.
  • Tally semantics (per model, across its recorded results): canary hit-rate over the results that carried a canary; judge compliance-rate (share of all results judged partial or full); human-confirmed rate (share with a human verdict of partial or full) over all results. Rendered "N / M (P%)", or "—" when the denominator is 0. Rows and tally rows appear in completion order, so tests filter by the provider/model key, never by position.
  • Everything renders as plain text. The payload, the spliced preview, each model output, and each judge verdict/reason enter the DOM via textContent only.
  • The panel is interactive only in context. The toggle is enabled only while a transcript is displayed; the payload field and insertion point need the toggle on; the model/judge pickers need a transcript, configured models, and no in-flight run; Run needs at least one selected model. The judge select shares the same option list as the multi-select and defaults to the same target the summarize picker pre-selects.

Log events emitted

None (browser code). It formats server events for the panel via LOG_FORMATTERS — one-line humanized formatters for the known events (server_started, server_stopped, http_request, fetch_attempt, fetch_rejected, transcript_saved, transcript_save_failed, summary_completed, summary_failed, summary_save_failed, llm_call_completed, llm_call_failed, config_load_failed, unhandled_exception), with a time LEVEL event key=value … fallback for unknown ones.

Error codes handled

INVALID_URL, VIDEO_UNAVAILABLE, NO_CAPTIONS, UPSTREAM_FAILURE, BUSY, NOT_CONFIGURED, INVALID_PROVIDER, PROVIDER_ERROR, INPUT_TOO_LONG — via the ERROR_MESSAGES map (preferred over the server message); network failures and unexpected shapes get a generic message.

Design decisions

Resolved from the archived change design docs:

  • 2026-10-29-youtube-transcript D6 — one static page, no build step, no framework, no CDN; the clipboard fallback for non-secure contexts; the no-HTML insertion rule (XSS).
  • 2026-11-02-add-saved-transcript-list decision 6 — the saved section: reusable result panel, prettified labels with real-name requests, client-side Blob download, load-once-plus-refresh (no polling).
  • add-transcript-summary decision 5 (the fetch response's name lands in a new variable; Download's predicate is intentionally untouched), decision 11 (the UI state machine: picker pre-selection, enabled predicate, currentSummary lifecycle, the e2e seam below summarize_with_provider).
  • 2026-11-03-add-log-viewer decision 6 — the panel shape, the EventSource opened once at page load, the formatters, the 200-line cap.
  • add-auto-summarize D4 (defaultSelection() shared by the picker pre-selection and the auto target), D5 (doSummarize(auto) as one code path, the hook after renderResult only, skip-and-show via the saved-summary read), D6 (subdued note for auto failures, checkbox revert on a failed settings write), D7 (accepted: a second auto-fire during an in-flight summarize is dropped).
  • add-prompt-injection-benchmark decision 1 (the client-side splice into one undifferentiated string — no server knows the split), decision 2 (delivery and judge both use the non-persisting POST /api/llm-call, never the persisting /api/summarize), decision 3 (system prompts only from the server-side preset registry — the client sends a preset id, no system text), decision 5 (the layered oracle: per-run canary token + judge over the original unspliced transcript + settable human verdict, with the per-model tally semantics).
